brief: I own Thistledown Ovens, a bakery in the village of Quillby, and I want a pre-order page for the weekend of 7 and 8 November 2026. Customers will open it from a link I paste into our neighbourhood chat group, nearly all on their phones. Items: sourdough loaf £5.20, cardamom bun six-pack £9.80, pear and walnut tart £14.50, rye crispbread bag £3.40, each from 0 to 6. They choose delivery or collection. Delivery is £3.50 inside Quillby and free when the items come to £30 or more; collection is free. They pick one window: Saturday 8:00 to 10:00, Saturday 10:00 to 12:00 (4 places left), Sunday 9:00 to 11:00, or Sunday 11:00 to 13:00 (full, show it but do not let them pick it). For delivery they can add a driver tip of none, 5%, 10%, 15% of the items, or an amount they type. They give a name, a phone number and any allergy note. Show a running basket with items, delivery, tip and total, then a last summary to confirm. Accent colour Wheat Gold #D9A441 on cream. When the link is shared it should read: Fresh bread and pastry for your weekend, delivered in Quillby.

Ticket sales for the Lanternfield Forum open on Monday 12 October 2026, and I need the checkout ready for buyers on a laptop at their desk, many buying for a whole team. The conference runs 18 and 19 November 2026 at the Harrowgate Assembly Rooms. Tickets: Early Bird £240 (until 31 October), Standard £320, Student £90 (student email address required) and Team Pack of five £1,100. Add-ons, chosen per person: Workshop day on 17 November £130 (11 of 40 places left), Speaker dinner on the 18th £75 (23 of 80 left), Printed programme with tote bag £15, and a year of Recording access £60. Team Pack buyers must enter five attendee names. The code TOWER10 takes 10% off tickets only, never add-ons. Every price includes 20% VAT, and the page should show how much of the total is VAT. The buyer picks how many of each ticket, ticks add-ons for each attendee, sees the total change as they go, and reviews a full order summary before confirming. Use Lantern Amber #E08A1E with near-black text. When the link is shared it should read: Two days of design talks in Harrowgate, with an optional workshop and dinner.

A customer, Ilse Brandvold, left her washing machine with us on 14 October 2026, and I need a quote she can open on her phone at work from a link in a text message. Machine: Halvex WM-7 front loader. Fault: loud grinding on spin and a leak at the door. What we found: drum bearing worn, door seal split, pump fine (filter was blocked; we cleaned it for free). Parts, each with an original and a cheaper compatible choice: drum bearing set £86 original or £48 compatible; door seal £39 original or £22 compatible. Original parts carry a 12-month guarantee, compatible ones 3 months. Labour is £65 an hour: bearing 2.5 hours, seal 0.5 hour, both together 2.75 hours. The £35 call-out and diagnosis fee is waived if she goes ahead and is charged if she declines. She should be able to say yes or no to each repair, choose original or compatible for each part, and watch the total update, with 20% VAT included. The quote is valid until 28 October 2026. At the end she approves it, or declines and collects the machine from Dunmere Repairs, 9 Cobblers Yard. Keep it friendly and plain. Use Dunmere Teal #1F6F6B.

It's Friday 23 October 2026 and I lead support at Tallybridge Invoicing. I need our open tickets triaged at the 9:30 stand-up, projected on the meeting-room screen for the four of us. Open tickets (ID, customer, subject, plan, age): T-4101, Alder Print Co, cannot log in after password reset, Business, 6 hours. T-4102, Birchall Dental, invoices sent twice to clients, Business, 2 days. T-4103, Teo Marchetti, how do I change my logo, Free, 3 days. T-4104, Greywater Bakehouse, charged twice for October, Business, 1 day. T-4105, Sable & Finch, request for recurring reminders, Pro, 9 days. T-4106, Dr Aanya Rao, export comes out blank, Pro, 4 hours. T-4107, Halden Freight, account locked after 5 attempts, Enterprise, 40 minutes. T-4108, Pim Verhoeven, thanks, all resolved, Free, 5 days. First-reply targets: Enterprise 1 hour, Business 4 hours, Pro 8 hours, Free 2 days; mark any ticket already past its target. For each ticket we set a priority (urgent, high, normal, low), an owner (Mirela for billing, Sunil for access, Tobias for the rest) and an action (reply now, escalate, snooze, close). Finish with a count per owner and a list of tickets with no decision yet.

Wednesday's release review for the Marlowe field-survey tool (version 3.8, shipping Thursday 12 November 2026) will be projected for the six of us, and afterwards I'll print the page as the record for the release committee. For each open bug I want us to record one decision: fix before release, ship with a known issue, defer to 3.9, or needs more information, plus a one-line reason. Bugs (ID, title, severity, share of users affected, workaround): MB-311, survey answers lost when the phone loses signal mid-save, data loss, about 4%, none. MB-318, app closes when opening a map with over 500 pins, crash, 2%, switch to list view. MB-322, date entry shows last year in January, minor, 1%, type the date. MB-327, sending a report by email fails when it has large photos, major, 9%, shrink the photos first. MB-330, warning message shows in the wrong colour, cosmetic, 100%, none. MB-334, GPS position is off by up to 30 m indoors, major, 12%, none. The rule: we cannot ship with any data loss or crash bug unless it is marked fix before release. Show a go or no-go at the top that updates as we decide, and list anything undecided. Colour: Signal Red #C0392B for no-go.

Harbourside Food Bank needs a sign-up page for volunteers for the week of 9 to 13 November 2026, and I'm the volunteer coordinator. People will open it from a link in our group chat, on their phones, usually in a spare minute. Shifts (day, time, role, places open out of places in total): Mon 9 Nov, 9:00 to 12:00, Sorting donations, 1 of 6. Mon 9 Nov, 11:00 to 14:00, Packing boxes, 4 of 5. Tue 10 Nov, 9:00 to 12:00, Driving (licence needed), 2 of 3. Wed 11 Nov, 17:00 to 20:00, Evening pantry desk, 0 of 4. Thu 12 Nov, 9:00 to 12:00, Sorting donations, 5 of 6. Fri 13 Nov, 13:00 to 16:00, Packing boxes, 3 of 5. I want volunteers to sort the list by most places open, by day, or by role, so the shifts that need people most are easy to find. Full shifts stay visible but cannot be chosen. A volunteer may take up to 3 shifts and cannot take two that overlap. They add their name and a phone number, see their chosen shifts, and confirm. Add a line saying volunteers must be 16 or over, and that anyone who cannot make a shift should message me, Rosalind, by 8:30 on the day. Colour: Harbour Blue #2A6F97.

I'm the platform engineer at Corvane Payments and before the change window on Tuesday 3 November 2026 I want one page that I open on my laptop to set which features are switched on in each environment: development, staging and production. Current state (feature, dev, staging, production): new-checkout-flow, on, on, off. saved-cards, on, on, on. instant-refunds, on, off, off. fraud-score-v2, on, on, on. emailed-receipts, off, off, off. bulk-payouts, on, on, off. Rules: a feature may be on in production only if it is on in staging; a feature may be on in staging only if it is on in development; fraud-score-v2 must stay on in production, always. I want to switch each one on or off in each environment, see a warning next to anything that breaks a rule, and see which switches differ from the current state. Finish with a plain change summary I can paste into the change ticket, one line per change, like staging: instant-refunds off to on. If nothing changed it should say so. Each change gets a short reason I type in. Tone: terse and exact; I will be reading it quickly on a deadline.

On Monday 2 November 2026 I present the rollout plan for same-day returns at Tarrow Parcel Co. to our leadership committee, who will each have a printed copy while I project it. Five regions, with customers: Northmarch 84,000, Saltreach 52,000, Eastvale 131,000, Highmoor 27,000, Lowfen 63,500. Three launch waves: Wave 1 on Monday 16 November, Wave 2 on Monday 30 November, Wave 3 on Monday 14 December 2026. The committee should switch each region on or off for the rollout and give it a wave, then see the customers covered after each wave and in total. Rules: no wave may exceed 150,000 customers (support capacity); Eastvale cannot be in Wave 1 because its depot is not trained until 24 November; nothing launches between 21 December and 4 January (freeze). Show a clear warning beside any plan that breaks a rule, and a one-line verdict on whether the plan is allowed. Put the risks in an appendix that people can skip: carrier delays (medium), staffing in Lowfen (high), label printer supply (low). Colour: Salt Grey #5C6B73 with a coral highlight #F4845F. When the link is shared it should read: How same-day returns reach five regions in three waves.

The cookie settings page for Atelier Mirabelle, my online candle shop, has to be written in French and has to work for customers on their phones the first time they visit. Make it calm and honest, and make refusing as easy as accepting. It shows three choices at the top, Tout accepter, Tout refuser and Choisir, and four categories: Nécessaires (always on, cannot be turned off; keeps the basket during the visit), Préférences (remembers language and delivery country for 12 months), Statistiques (counts visits without names, for 13 months), Publicité (shows our candles on other sites, for 6 months). Every optional category starts off. Each category gets a one-sentence explanation, in plain French, of what it does and for how long. After the customer saves, show a clear recap of what is on and off and the date, plus a line saying they can change their mind at any time. Last updated 2 November 2026. Colour: Mirabelle Plum #5B2A5F on warm white. When the link is shared it should read: Vos choix de cookies chez Atelier Mirabelle, simples et modifiables à tout moment.

I lead developer relations at Pebblewick Notes, a note-taking product, and I want a page my writers open on laptops to build the instruction we give an AI model when it turns a raw list of changes into release notes. The instruction, with slots in capitals: You write release notes for PRODUCT VERSION, dated DATE, for AUDIENCE. Tone: TONE. Group the changes under New, Improved and Fixed. Give each change one line of at most WORDS words. Do not invent changes. Changes: CHANGES. The writer fills each slot, and the page shows the finished instruction ready to copy. Also show these three filled samples, each as a finished instruction, so writers see the range: (1) Pebblewick Notes 2.4.1, 9 November 2026, everyday users, calm, 14 words, changes: fixed a crash when pasting images; search is faster. (2) Pebblewick Notes 2.5.0, 23 November 2026, team admins, friendly, 18 words, changes: shared folders; export a whole notebook; fixed duplicate reminders. (3) Pebblewick Notes 3.0.0, 7 December 2026, developers, precise, 22 words, changes: new add-on system; old sync removed; faster start. Warn if any slot is empty.

As head of people at Corrin Valley Hospital, I want a page for our hiring panels, opened on a laptop and then printed for the panel table, that builds the instruction we give an AI model to write interview questions. The instruction, with slots in capitals: Write COUNT interview questions for the role of ROLE at Corrin Valley Hospital, level: LEVEL. Focus on COMPETENCY. Make each question STYLE. After each question give one follow-up and a short note on what a strong answer contains. Never ask about age, family, health, religion or nationality. The panel picks each slot: COUNT from 3 to 10; LEVEL from newly qualified, experienced or lead; ROLE typed in, for example night-shift charge nurse; COMPETENCY from patient safety, handover, conflict, teamwork or leadership under pressure; STYLE from situational or about past experience. The panel has 40 minutes and allows 5 minutes per question including the follow-up, so show the time used and warn if the questions will not fit. Start with this example already filled in: 5, experienced, night-shift charge nurse, handover, about past experience. The finished instruction is shown in full, ready to copy.

Our customer care team at Brindle & Fell, an outdoor gear shop, answers about 300 messages a day, and I want a reply helper that each of our six agents uses on a laptop between tickets. The agent picks a situation, a tone and a length, types the customer's first name and order number, and sees a finished reply to copy. Situations: late parcel (new delivery date Thursday 19 November 2026, apology voucher code FELL5 for £5 off); damaged item (free replacement or full refund, their choice, photo needed within 7 days); wrong size (free return label, exchange within 14 days). Tones, each with its greeting and sign-off: Warm, 'Hi NAME, thank you so much for your patience' and 'Take care, Brindle & Fell Care'. Plain, 'Hello NAME' and 'Regards, Brindle & Fell Care'. Formal, 'Dear NAME' and 'Yours sincerely, Brindle & Fell Care'. Lengths: Short about 40 words, Standard about 90, Full about 160. Show the actual word count of the reply and flag it if it is more than 15 words from the length chosen. Never promise anything that is not listed here. Keep it plain and quick to use; agents are working through a queue.
